Estimate motif-specific on-target mutation rates using prior probability

Source: R/estimate_inference_with_prior.R
estimate_inference_with_prior.Rd

estimate_inference_with_prior performs motif-aware inference using motif prior probabilities, and estimates site-level mutation or conversion signal along with posterior probabilities.

Usage

estimate_inference_with_prior(
  chr.info,
  treatment_fixed_count,
  control_fixed_count,
  treatment_depth,
  control_depth,
  motif_specific = TRUE,
  delta = 0.001,
  depth.cutoff = 10,
  homo.cutoff = 0.99,
  bg.method = "fisher",
  highly.methyl.cutoff = 0.95,
  ref.freq.tab = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  thread = 1,
  motif = "DRACH",
  Nmer = "5mer"
)

Arguments

chr.info

A data.frame with three columns: site position in the format "chrom_coordinate_strand" (e.g., chr1_14404_-), site motif sequence (e.g., AAACC), and site motif type (e.g., NNUNN).

treatment_fixed_count

A vector of non-mutation counts for each site in the treatment sample.

control_fixed_count

A vector of non-mutation counts for each site in the control sample.

treatment_depth

A vector of read coverage for each site in the treatment sample.

control_depth

A vector of read coverage for each site in the control sample.

motif_specific

Logical. Whether to estimate on-target mutation rates by motif. If FALSE, one overall mutation rate is estimated. Default is TRUE.

delta

The sequencing error rate. Default is 0.001.

depth.cutoff

The minimum read coverage for each site in the treatment and control sample. Default is 10.

homo.cutoff

The minimum ratio of non-mutation counts for each site in the control sample that is used to determine homozygous sites. Default is 0.99.

bg.method

The statistical test to infer the background sites. One of "binomial", "fisher", "lrt". Default is "fisher".

highly.methyl.cutoff

The upper quantile cutoff of candidate signal sites used for estimating on-target mutation rates. This argument name is retained for backward compatibility. Default is 0.95.

ref.freq.tab

A data.frame with motif frequencies in signal and background sets, plus the prior probability of each motif sequence. This table can be created by compute_prior and must contain the columns "motif" and "prior_methylated".

seed

A seed for the random number generators.

thread

A positive integer numeric specifying the number of cores for parallel computing. Default is 1.

motif

The target 5-mer motif pattern. MIRAGE expands supported degenerate bases internally. The default is "DRACH"; set this explicitly for the assay being analyzed.

Nmer

The strategy for further grouping motifs. One of "5mer", "f4mer" or "l4mer". "5mer" will not consider further grouping strategy. In the "f4mer" and "l4mer" mode, all 5-mer motifs are grouped by sharing the same first or last 4-mer sequences, respectively. The argument is only used if motif_specific = TRUE.

Value

A list including a data.frame of homozygous sites, a data.frame of heterozygous sites, a data.frame of estimated on-target mutation rates for each motif (lambda1), and the estimated background mutation rate (lambda2).

Details

estimate_inference_with_prior estimates site-level signal from motif prior probabilities, which are usually obtained by compute_prior. The count table can be generated by any preprocessing pipeline as long as it contains site IDs, motif annotations, treatment and control fixed-base counts, and treatment and control read depths in the expected order.

Examples

# Estimate signal levels from a PAR-CLIP count table with motif priors.
count_table <- read.delim(system.file("extdata", "pos.read.count.example.parclip.txt",
                                      package = "MIRAGE"))

motif_counts <- table(count_table$motif)
motif_freq_exp <- data.frame(motif = names(motif_counts),
                             freq = as.numeric(motif_counts) / sum(motif_counts))
motif_freq_bg <- data.frame(motif = names(motif_counts),
                            tx_count = as.numeric(motif_counts),
                            genome_count = as.numeric(motif_counts))
motif_prior <- compute_prior(motif_freq_exp, motif_freq_bg, target_motif = "NNUNN",
                             target_base_index = 3, prob_methylation = 0.01)

res <- with(count_table, estimate_inference_with_prior(cbind(pos, motif, type),
            treated_fixed_count, control_fixed_count, treated_depth, control_depth,
            motif_specific = FALSE, delta = 0.001, depth.cutoff = 10,
            highly.methyl.cutoff = 0.95, ref.freq.tab = motif_prior,
            seed = 123, thread = 1, motif = "NNUNN", Nmer = "5mer"))
#> Considering 989 (99%) sites as homozygous...
#> Considering 887 (89.69%) sites as background (homozygous sites only)...
#> Considering 8 (0.81%) sites as high-signal site candidates (homozygous sites only)...
head(res$homosites[, c("pos", "motif", "beta_est", "posterior")])
#>              pos motif       beta_est posterior
#> 1 chr1_1233912_+ ACUUU 0.000001006474 0.9978190
#> 2 chr1_1233913_+ CUUUC 0.000001006474 0.9978190
#> 3 chr1_1233914_+ UUUCC 0.062045505136 0.9960682
#> 4 chr1_1233917_+ CCUUU 0.037124010384 0.9969108
#> 5 chr1_1233918_+ CUUUC 0.161731496908 0.9907397
#> 6 chr1_1233919_+ UUUCA 0.037124010384 0.9969108
